recipes.name: Mike’s Peppered Beef Jerky
ingredients_raw: 4 pounds very lean beef, visible fat trimmed and cut against the grain into 1/4 inch-thick strips
1 teaspoon liquid smoke, or more to taste
0.25 teaspoon ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Place beef strips on a solid, level surface. Firmly pound beef with the tenderizing side of a meat mallet until the meat fibers are slightly broken but the strips still hold their shape.
Mix Worcestershire sauce, soy sauce, brown sugar, onion powder, garlic powder, black pepper, liquid smoke, cayenne pepper, and coriander seeds in a large bowl until brown sugar has dissolved.
Place beef strips into the bowl; add enough water to allow marinade to cover the meat. Stir to incorporate water and submerge the beef in marinade, cover the bowl, and refrigerate for 24 hours.
Preheat oven to 300 degrees F (150 degrees C).
Remove beef strips from marinade, shake off excess, and lay the strips onto oven-proof racks. Do not overlap the strips.
Bake the beef strips in the preheated oven until an instant-read thermometer inserted into the thickest strip reads at least 150 degrees F (65 degrees C).
Remove strips from oven and place onto racks of a food dehydrator so the strips don’t overlap.
If desired, sprinkle strips with more coriander seeds and black pepper.

Turn on the dehydrator, set machine’s temperature for 155 degrees F (70 degrees C), and dry the jerky until leathery, about 9 hours. Rotate the racks from top to bottom every 1 1/2 hours for even drying. A piece of jerky should crack but not break in half when folded.

raw_recipe.headline: Mike’s Peppered Beef Jerky
raw_recipe.description: Slowly-marinated beef strips dry into savory pieces of peppery beef jerky in a food dehydrator. For safety, it’s best to cook the strips first before drying.

review.reviewBody: When I submitted this recipe step 6 was not included. I use only my dehydrater for drying and not the oven, this is why the time may be shorter.

Great recipe! I have made this half a dozen times and suggest a few small tweaks. I add 1/2 tsp crushed red pepper and 1/2 tsp white pepper as well as a tablespoon of Blues Hog Smokey Mountain BBQ sauce. 5 hours at 158 degrees in the magic mill and it comes out great.

made this yesterday...dh said it was great!!! only thing i did was 1/2 the recipe...used trimmed sirloin...will forsure make it again...thanks mike!!! ;o) ps i used my smoker (hickory & whiskey wood chips for about 4 hours on really low 200 degree heat) yummo

Great recipe. I added a heck of a lot of cracked red pepper to spice it up. We didn't have the Liquid Smoke. Also, we didn't precook it in the oven - just placed it in our dehydrator at 155 degrees for about 7 hours. Turned out amazing!

got dehydrator at a yardsale for 4.00 thought use once , lol heck my hubby loves it ,,better then you buy at store , and it never last more then a few days , make chicken for dogs too , with pnut butter, i didnt use oven just right in to dehydrator , once it marinated all nite, took about 9 hours , hubby said is it done yet , have made mikes 6 times in 3 months , better then u buy at stores and fresh,I added 1/2 teaspoon tabasco , and 1/2 teaspoon of A-1 , hubby likes it hot , never had dehydrated anything before mikes recipe is so easy , even for me , add other ingredients to taste,experiment , ty vm MIKE,,,,,even i could do it ,,,getting ready to make another batch for thanksgiving ,

This was my first time making jerky in my new dehydrator. I chose this recipe over doc's with the video because so far you rated all 5 stars, so, good place to start. I used a4.5 lb London broil cut at 1/8 inch. Only changed out of necessity, used smoked paprika instead of liquid smoke b/c I was out, and no coriander.

It only took 4 hours in my dehydrator. Spice was perfect. Hubby and boys were amazed. I need to experiment some more but I will come back to this recipe for sure! Thanks Mike.
Made this with a little more cayenne, and it was a huge success. First time making jerky in my smoker and you can count more of this recipe :)
This stuff tastes just like the kind I buy in the store,but BETTER! I doubled the pepper and it tastes awesome! Thanks for the recipe.

This is my go to jerky recipe. I've made it a dozen times or more, and it's great every time. The only change I made was to only use 2 pounds of beef, to get more of the flavor. I like a strong flavored jerky. Thanks for the recipe!

We made this for Christmas as gifts for our diabetic relatives...and the rest of us jerky lover's too. It was fabulous. The leaner the beef the shorter the dehydrator time and the safer the finished product. We used round steak, but found it still too fatty. We will use top round or some other type of leaner beef next time. However, the flavor was perfect..and no nitrites like store-bought jerky. Much cheaper too! We did not change anything in this recipe. Thanks Mike.

The dehydrator and the oven made the beef extremely dry. Plus, I over used the black pepper. I have now seen Mikes addition about only using dehydrator for drying. Another than my mistakes for dehydrating and over use of black pepper, the recipe smelled awesome marinating. I won't make the same mistake next time.

Very good! We hike a lot so I’m always looking for good food I can take without all the processed stuff… I made marinade as stated except I didn’t have coriander. Marinated in bag overnight. Patted with paper towel to remove excess marinade and popped in dehydrator at 150 for 6 hours. Easy and delish!
i have made this recipe for my sons there all first responders and there not 1 person that hasn't Loved this recipe i buy 30 lbs of roast at a time
Even if you like cilantro, beware of the coriander because you may get that soap taste. I was shocked and ruined my entire batch because it tastes like Dawn dish soap.

This is by far the best recipe I've tried to date. And I've tried many. I wouldn't change a thing about it
Delicious. Didn't use coriander but that was just my choice.
no changes, will not do this one again just because it was too peppery for my liking. Could try it with less pepper.
